thread.title_full: Missouri State Board of Education approves A-F grade card framework and FY 2028 budget

author: E. M. Blum
title: Missouri State Board of Education approves A-F grade card framework and FY 2028 budget
text:
Missouri State Board of Education approves A–F grade card framework and FY 2028 budget
By E. M. Blum
The Missouri State Board of Education approved the Department of Elementary and Secondary Education’s proposed A–F Grade Card Framework and Fiscal Year 2028 budget request during its meeting on Sept. 15.
School leaders from Monett R‑I, Oran R‑III, Pattonville R‑III, and Joplin Schools addressed the board with recommendations for the A–F grade card rollout. They suggested a pilot year to review draft grades, delaying the literacy measure until 2026–27, keeping statewide test windows open until mid-May, and maintaining current data-validation timelines. Leaders also said that raising grading thresholds when 65% of schools earn an A or B would create a forced curve that does not accurately reflect improvement. They emphasized that A–F grades should not be mistaken for accreditation, and asked the board to use its authority to modify implementation timelines.
The State Board approved implementation of the proposed grading framework as required by Executive Order 26-01. This allows DESE to prepare data for publication, develop a technical guide, and set a pilot timeframe using 2024–25 data. The framework is intended to provide families with a straightforward view of school performance based on academic achievement, value-added growth, growth to proficiency, success-ready graduate indicators, and graduation rates. During discussion, board members asked how poverty impacts student outcomes within this system and whether piloting should occur before full statewide implementation. In response to these concerns, DESE said growth measures in the framework are designed to reflect improvement regardless of economic status or starting point on proficiency scales. The department will conduct a pilot before public release.
Dr. Kyle Kruse and Rebecca Jackson presented DESE’s FY 2028 budget request, which includes new decision items as well as supplemental requests for early childhood programs and high-need special education initiatives. The board approved all portions except for the foundation formula request; it directed that this remain at FY 2027 levels ($4,282,736,000), approximately $270 million less than what is needed for full funding.
St. Louis Public Schools Superintendent Dr. Myra Berry briefed the board on district progress in attendance (with goals to increase from 52.5% to 82.5% by 2028), literacy efforts such as expanded phonics instruction and tutoring programs, and financial improvements including enhanced controls and planning systems resulting in a fund balance above fifty percent.
Other actions included approving an amendment regarding child care subsidy eligibility rules (5 CSR 25‑200.060) and authorizing a five-year charter application for North County Innovative School (NCIS). The next State Board meeting is scheduled for October 20 in Jefferson City.
The Missouri Department of Elementary and Secondary Education supports school accountability through the Missouri School Improvement Program; serves all public school districts across Missouri; manages K-12 education along with early childhood initiatives; coordinates federal programs such as Title I funding; operates under leadership from its Commissioner; oversees both traditional districts and charter schools statewide according to the official website.
